title: Polynomial quotient fields over a relatively algebraically closed subfield
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] such that every $x\in K$ algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] is the image of an element of $k$. Let $P\in k[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] be monic and irreducible, where monic means leading coefficient $1$ and irreducible means nonzero, not a unit, with a unit factor in every factorization. Let $P_K\in K[T]$ be its coefficientwise image [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map]. Then $P_K$ is irreducible, and $K[T]/(P_K)$ is a nonzero field; here $(P_K)$ is the ideal of all multiples of $P_K$. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}(K[T]/(P_K))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has exactly one point and is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. No separability assumption on $P$ and no finite-generation assumption on $K/k$ is made.

source.place: Tag 037P (lemma-field-extension-geometrically-irreducible), proof, monic factor normalization, coefficient descent and the quotient-field argument (old steps 4 and 5)

proof.text: Identify $k$ with its image in $K$ using [def-pc-field-extension]. The coefficient formula in [def-weil-polynomial-ring] shows that for nonzero polynomials the highest nonzero product coefficient is the product of their leading coefficients. Thus degrees add over a field, and the units are exactly the nonzero constants. Since $P$ is monic and not a unit, its coefficientwise image $P_K$ is monic of the same positive degree [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map], hence nonzero and not a unit. For an arbitrary factorization $P_K=AB$, both factors are nonzero. Put $a=\operatorname{lc}(A)$, $b=\operatorname{lc}(B)$; then $ab=1$. Set $Q=a^{-1}A$ and $R=aB$. Their leading coefficients are $1$, and $QR=P_K$.

source.place: Tag 037P (lemma-field-extension-geometrically-irreducible), proof: normalize a hypothetical factorization to monic factors

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-monic-divisor-algebraic-coefficients] separately to the monic divisors $Q$ and $R$ of $P_K$. Every coefficient is algebraic over $k$, hence lies in $k$ by the assumption that every element of $K$ algebraic over $k$ is the image of an element of $k$. Choose its unique preimage under $k\hookrightarrow K$; zero has preimage zero, so these coefficient lists still have finite support. They define monic polynomials $Q_0,R_0\in k[T]$ whose images are $Q,R$. The coefficientwise map is injective because $k\to K$ is injective [def-pc-field-extension], and is multiplicative [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map]. Applying this to $QR=P_K$ gives $P=Q_0R_0$.

source.place: Tag 037P proof, coefficient descent by Tag 00H6 (lemma-polynomials-divide), clause (1)

proof.text: Irreducibility of $P$ implies that $Q_0$ or $R_0$ is a unit. Mapping its inverse along the ring homomorphism of [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map] shows that $Q$ or $R$ is a unit. Multiplication by the nonzero constant $a$ or $a^{-1}$ preserves being a unit, so $A$ or $B$ is a unit. Together with the nonzero, nonunit assertions in Step 1, this proves irreducibility of $P_K$ for every factorization.

source.place: Tag 037P proof, contradiction with irreducibility over k

proof.text: Put $F=P_K$ and $I=(F)$. The ideal $I$ is proper: $1=FH$ would make $F$ a unit. By [lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid], every ideal $J$ of $K[T]$ containing $I$ is principal, say $J=(G)$. Since $F\in J$, write $F=GH$. Irreducibility gives that $G$ or $H$ is a unit. In the first case $J=K[T]$; in the second $G=FH^{-1}$, so $J=I$. Thus $I$ is maximal. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field] to the commutative ring $K[T]$ and this maximal ideal to conclude that $K[T]/I$ is a field, in particular a nonzero ring.

source.place: Tag 037P proof, quotient-field justification for the spectrum conclusion; polynomial PID input from Tag 030A (lemma-polynomial-domain-normal), proof opening

proof.text: By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the spectrum of the field $K[T]/I$ has exactly one point. It is nonempty, and in any closed cover of this singleton one of the two closed subsets contains its point and hence is the whole space. This is irreducibility by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. None of the preceding steps used separability of $P$ or finite generation of $K/k$.
